I have been going to Goolds for over 10 years and, for many of those years, I was very happy with the care and the personal service we received.

Unfortunately, since Village Vets Co-operation took over, I feel the practice has become much more impersonal. I called in last week and was disappointed that the lady at the desk hardly looked up when she spoke to me. It may seem like a small thing, but after being a client for over 10 years, that lack of warmth really stood out to me.

I have also since heard that Conor has left the practice, which is another real shame.

Thankfully, someone told me that some of the old Goolds staff have opened Marina Vets. It is reassuring to know that there is somewhere that still values the personal connection with clients and their pets.

It’s sad to see a practice that once felt so familiar and welcoming change so much. After more than 10 years, I never expected to feel like just another customer.

I am absolutely delighted with Víctor. You can really tell he is a veterinarian who truly loves animals. He gave my kitten, Milky, a thorough check-up to ensure he didn't have any fractures or broken bones. On top of that, he speaks Spanish, which made the appointment much easier. It was a wonderful experience having him care for Milky, and I completely recommend him for your pets. He is an outstanding vet who genuinely cares. I’m thrilled with both the clinic and Víctor. This is a true story that happened to me. I am confined to a wheelchair after falling from a horse. Last Monday, I went to this Veterinary Clinic because my service dog, a female Labrador, was experiencing severe shortness of breath. She was given a Dimazon injection, and her condition improved. On Tuesday, she received another Dimazon injection. On Wednesday, they performed a heart scan, and everything seemed fine. Her attending veterinarian, Conor, later sent me a text message saying that her blood tests also came back normal. However, on Saturday evening, she started struggling to breathe again. After midnight, I desperately searched for an open veterinary clinic in Cork. I drove to three different clinics, but none of them were open. An hour after we returned home, unsuccessful in finding help, my beloved dog took her last breath. When I messaged Dr. Conor about what had happened, he apologized, admitting that he hadn’t been able to make a more accurate diagnosis. But all it would have taken was a single diuretic tablet, and my amazing service dog might still be alive today.
